title: Contextual writing review and measured execution cost

baseline.limits: The scanner finds lexical candidates for eight rules. Prompt composition does not execute or validate model analysis. Hosts own model configuration, durable decisions and source writes.

functions.problem: A lexical match cannot decide whether a page serves its reader or whether an explanation is necessary.
functions.input: Audience, reader task, genre, language, versioned text units, approved claims and prior decisions.
functions.output: A bounded context object identifying authoritative facts, source material, constraints and missing context.
acceptance: Preserve the distinction between source text and host instructions.
Identify missing reader goals instead of inventing them.
Keep input source versions and accepted decisions traceable.
Include short UI labels, public documentation and positive keep cases in EN/DE evaluation.

functions.problem: A model can invent quotes, offsets, rule coverage or evidence even when its prose sounds convincing.
functions.input: Unknown model output, the selected rule set, exact source snapshot and permitted evidence IDs.
functions.output: Validated advisory findings or structured validation failures, plus explicit reviewed and unreviewed scope.
acceptance: Reject unknown rule/evidence IDs and mismatched quotes.
Validate UTF-16 positions after emoji and German characters.
Reject stale or ambiguous source assignments.
Distinguish an empty valid result from incomplete, malformed or failed analysis.

functions.problem: One call per rule repeats source and instructions; an unbounded combined prompt can dilute attention or exceed the context budget.
functions.input: Versioned units, review context, selected rule IDs and a host-supplied request budget.
functions.output: Review jobs grouped by compatible goal, language and rule scope, retaining per-unit IDs and coverage.
acceptance: Compare six separate rules with the same six rules combined.
Do not discard semantic review because lexical scanning found no match.
Keep whole-page context available across chunk boundaries.
Avoid duplicate findings when jobs overlap.
Never choose a provider, credential or paid fallback from repository policy.
Take route and token limits from the host; obtain fresh capacity/admission for every executed attempt, including retries.
Preserve evidence-cohort and Voice qualification checks; pure job planning grants no model execution permission.

functions.problem: Character counts, cache assumptions and model prices can misrepresent the actual cost of a review.
functions.input: Canonically resolved route, Token Economy price resolution/version, UTC execution date, serialized jobs, identified tokenizer and output/reasoning limits.
functions.output: Usage estimates or explicit unknown values, shared price/cost resolution and reconciliation with provider-reported usage. The host enforces the spending ceiling.
acceptance: Never present UTF-8 bytes or character estimates as measured model tokens.
Account for cache writes, cache reads, output/reasoning and relevant context tiers.
Require a host prelaunch check before any launch or retry that could exceed the authorized ceiling.
Record retries and unsuccessful paid attempts.
Report cost per accepted complete review as the primary economic result; include every attempt once and report useful findings separately.
Extend missing pricing dimensions in Token Economy or return unsupported; do not maintain a parallel Voice runtime price catalogue.

functions.packageProposal: Voice adapters for Token Economy benchmark contracts
functions.problem: A shorter prompt or a cheaper model may lose relevant findings or rewrite legitimate wording.
functions.input: Git-owned labelled cases and prompt versions mapped to BenchmarkDefinition/IBenchmarkInvoker, exact canonically resolved routes and explicit host experiment admission.
functions.output: Reproducible results with precision/recall by selected rule and locale, harmful edits, abstentions, latency, usage and cost.
acceptance: Separate deterministic local measurements from model results.
Preserve negative examples and deliberately acceptable wording.
Compare equivalent rule coverage before claiming savings.
Use blinded human adjudication and a held-out set for effectiveness claims.
Record unavailable models and failed requests without substituting another model silently.
Reuse BenchmarkRunner and RoutingEvidenceAggregator/Report with explicit Voice locale/profile and meaning-preservation gates.
Preserve unknown usage and allocate attempt cost once when deriving per-finding metrics from accepted-delivery evidence.
Compare model and prompt organization on paired cases; separate quality from price and keep the no-change outcome eligible for acceptance.

functions.problem: A rewrite can turn limited evidence into assured outcomes or attach a source that does not support the claim.
functions.input: Exact claims, approved evidence excerpts, source identifiers and the review context.
functions.output: Supported, unsupported or unresolved claim assessments with quoted evidence and missing facts.
acceptance: Preserve numerical and causal qualifications.
Do not treat a valid URL or a model's agreement as proof of support.
Allow unresolved outcomes when evidence is absent.
Evaluate both original and proposed wording against the same facts.

functions.problem: Several fluent rewrites may repeat the same framing, add unsupported claims or weaken a strong original.
functions.input: Original passage, one to three proposals, reader goal, evidence and accepted decisions.
functions.output: A comparison of task fit, factual preservation, distinctness and reasons to keep the original.
acceptance: Compare alternatives at similar lengths where possible.
Recognize paraphrases that offer no material choice.
Do not fill a requested count with weak alternatives.
Retain deliberate contrasts, rhythms and terminology when they serve the goal.

functions.problem: Repeated review can undo intentional wording or treat agreement with the requester as sufficient evidence.
functions.input: Host-provided keep/accept/edit decisions, reasons, source versions and updated context.
functions.output: Applicable decision constraints and decisions requiring renewed review after source or context changes.
acceptance: Reuse existing Studio decision records through a host adapter.
Keep durable storage and authorization with the host.
Do not suppress unrelated findings after a keep decision.
Distinguish retained author intent from factual validation.

functions.problem: Pages may individually read well while repeating the same framing or contradicting terminology, positioning and claims across the project.
functions.input: Explicitly selected Git or working-copy snapshots, page goals, approved terminology, claims and decisions.
functions.output: Cross-file findings with source locators, compared evidence and bounded follow-up tasks.
acceptance: Pin each context repository independently, including marketing sources.
Identify cross-page contradictions without rewriting files.
Keep SEO and visual checks as separately reported capabilities.
Avoid claiming complete project coverage from a partial file selection.

functions.problem: Existing prose tools have different scopes, positions, language coverage, licenses and proposed-fix semantics.
functions.input: Named engine/version, native diagnostics, exact source and its parsed prose mapping.
functions.output: Voice findings retaining engine IDs, original messages, verified spans, proposed fixes and coverage limits.
acceptance: Qualify one adapter before adding a broad engine catalogue.
Preserve markup-aware input required by the engine.
Convert offsets explicitly and test Unicode, quotes and code exclusions.
Check selected rule-pack licenses separately.
Never interpret an engine match as AI authorship or automatic source-write permission.

ownership.voice: Rubrics, authored fixtures, locale/profile cohorts and editorial acceptance criteria.
ownership.tokenEconomy: Canonical model/provider/CLI identities, dated price knowledge, general routing and benchmark evidence.
ownership.host: Admission, credentials, hard prelaunch budgets, capacity and actual execution.

gaps: ModelPrice has input/output/cache-read/cache-write rates and validity dates; Batch, long-context tiers, cache TTL/storage need explicit shared modelling or an unsupported result.
ComputeCost currently falls back to input rates for missing cache rates; unknown provider-specific charges must remain explicit rather than silently declared accurate.
BenchmarkRunner checks CostCaps after InvokeAsync; a host guard is required for a hard prelaunch or total spend ceiling.
Benchmark token usage is not nullable; preserve unknown usage through an adapter or shared contract extension rather than supplying zero.
OutcomeEfficiency measures accepted deliveries. Define the review-to-delivery mapping and allocate each attempt cost once, even when it produces several findings.
RequiredBenchmarkCapability selects an evidence cohort; validate the actual chosen route and provisional experiment admission separately.
BenchmarkRunner.Compare orders success rate, primary outcome, token count and latency, not actual monetary efficiency; use accepted-review outcome and cost evidence for economic selection.
The concrete CLI benchmark invokers request broad filesystem permissions and coerce missing usage to zero. Reuse the read-only Voice Runner boundary and preserve unknown usage instead.

economicObjective.primary: Minimize observed total cost per accepted complete review, subject to predeclared meaning/fact preservation, false-change, missed-issue and latency criteria for the exact locale/profile cohort.
comparisonAxes: One rule, related rule groups, fixed profile and complete-catalogue prompts
Cheap-first escalation with independently audited non-escalated cases
economicObjective.constraint: A spending ceiling bounds execution; it does not select the best model or prompt. Research candidates remain unqualified until comparable model results exist.
